text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.

- The European Christian Democratic Union (EUCD) severed ties with Hungary's Christian Democratic People's Party (KDNP), on Friday, citing its unacceptable links with the far-right Hungarian Justice and Life Party (MIEP).

- The government considers a real wage increase of 1.5 to 2 percent realistic next year, but employee representatives envisage 4.5 to 5 percent, a Monday meeting of the Interest Coordination Council heard.

- The EU has no time to squander before the start of membership negotiations, Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker, who holds the EU's rotating presidency, told reporters after his Monday meeting with Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn. Juncker expressed hope that the talks would begin by early 1998.

- The average personal income tax burden may drop by up to 0.2 percent next year, as 25 percent of pension contributions may be deducted from the tax base, Finance Ministry deputy state secretary Peter Csobanczy told a conference on Monday
- Car dealers sold a total of 27,939 cars in Hungary in the first half of the year, excluding Suzuki sales, the Association of Hungarian Car Importers reports.

- The clothing industry is expected to stagnate this year, although the textile sector has a good change of growing 2 to 3 percent this year, the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism said on Monday.

- The Health Insurance Fund is expected to close this year with a deficit of 40 billion forints, according to analysts' forecasts, while the government puts this figure to 20 billion to 22 billion forints.

- Foreign investors held 49.3 of the 218.917 billion forints combined registered capital of banks in Hungary last year, the annual report by the State Banking and Capital Market Supervision (APTF) reveals.

- All seven parliamentary parties have reached a preliminary agreement in favor of the government's proposal to limit campaign spending for the spring 1998 elections to 386 million forints per party, or one million forint per candidate.
- Hungary's food exports grew 6.2 percent in the first five months, while imports increased 8.5 percent, the Industry, Trade and Tourism Ministry reveals.

- In its last plenary session before summer break the Parliament will vote today on a resolution to help alleviate damage and assist the victims of massive floods in countries to the north, and is expected to approve a draft resolution on NATO membership. (VILAGGAZDASAG as well).

- Hungayr would abandon its parctice of considering the cases of only those refugees and asylum seekes from European countries, under a bill unanimously approved for consideration on Monday by the Parliament's Constitution and Justice Committee (MAGYAR HIRLAP as well).
